author: claude-opus-5-5 SME critic (independent Claude critic subagent, 2026-11-19)

findings.claim: Endless animations on the tags or the checklist are read before their first frame. Since loop 6 that lets short, undelayed endless scale, rotate and checklist animations pass in most runs, which loop 5 rejected every time. The test's outcome also changes from run to run on identical bytes. Mechanism: line 142 finishes only finite animations, so endless ones are read 'as drawn'. In the pinned Chromium (HeadlessChrome 140.0.7339.186) that read usually happens before the first animation frame. Replaying the test's own flow (900x800 page, goto, then the 800x800 and 1280x1000 reads) on two endless-animation pages, 9 of 12 reads saw the animations still pending with currentTime 0, and the other three at about 16-33 ms. Part that is new in loop 6: at time 0 an endless animation whose first keyframe is identity computes to scale '1' or rotate '0deg'. The strict 'none' comparison used to reject those strings, and identity() (lines 146-152, 198) now accepts them. Reproduced on a git archive of 89161df6 with the private completed work plus one added rule each, full suite, 10 runs each. An endless alternating scale from 1 upward on both tags passed all 12 in 9 of 10 runs. An endless 4s linear rotate spin passed in 8 of 10, and an endless 0.5s pulse to half size with only a to keyframe in 9 of 10. An endless transform rotate spin passed in 7 of 10, and an endless pulse of .site-aside from scale 1 downward in 10 of 10. At ea630d09 the same five rules failed task 11 in every run: 3 of 3 each, with earlier rounds adding 5 of 5 for the scale-from-1 and rotate-spin rules and 4 of 4 for the pulse and transform-spin rules. An endless animation whose first keyframe is not identity fails 10 of 10 at 89161df6, which confirms the instant-of-reading mechanism. Part that is older than loop 6: the same read also lets undelayed endless animations of other box properties pass at both commits. An endless 0.5s alternating animation of .pack-tag-day's width passed all 12 in 3 of 5 runs at 89161df6 and 3 of 5 at ea630d09. One of .pack-tag-overnight's padding passed in 4 of 5 and 5 of 5. So 'slow' is not what lets an endless animation through. Its state at the moment of reading is. The unmodified spin page, sampled at 0.3s, 1s, 2.2s, 3.5s and 6.5s, draws the day tag outside the 0.5px tolerance at every sample. Consequences: cl4-sme-001 variant (b), an infinite scale animation on both tags, passes again, and a grader can get a different outcome on the same page. The lab.json notes sentence 'an endless animation is measured as drawn' implies endless animations are caught. The solved-run record lists 'an endless scale animation' among variants that each failed task 11, and that cannot be reproduced for an endless animation that starts at identity. Neither the lab.json residual list ('a paused, delayed or very long one') nor the record's ('paused, long-delayed, very long or slow animations and animated custom properties') includes short, undelayed endless animations. README line 17 ('does not catch every animation') and line 141 (keep the assessed layout static) still cover the case in general terms, so a learner who follows the README is not misled. Medium, graded like cl4-sme-001 and cl5-sme-001: a wrong page passes, but only after a deliberate keyframes rule, and the calculated width is still required. It is made worse by being partly a regression and nondeterministic.

evidence.section: 4.4.6 Waiting for the associated effect (non-normative: Web Animations typically begins timing an animation from the moment its first frame is complete, represented by an unresolved start time that becomes resolved when the animation is ready) and 4.4.4 Setting the current time of an animation (the current time can be set to seek the animation)

findings.recommendation: Make the reading of endless animations deterministic, without a keyframe classifier. Primary fix: before reading, seek each endless animation on the checklist and the tags to fixed, non-zero offsets inside its first active iteration (for example a quarter, a half and three quarters of the iteration after its delay). Read at each offset, then restore the original current time. That covers width, padding and transform alike. Narrower fix that only removes the loop-6 part: accept identity values only on an element whose animations are all finished after line 142, and keep the loop-5 strict comparison (transform, scale, rotate and translate exactly 'none', zoom '1') while an animation is still running. I verified the narrower fix on a work-dir copy of the test, applied to both the tag check and the checklist check. All six endless transform-type variants above failed task 11 in 5 of 5 runs each, the checklist one with the checklist message. These passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs each: the completed work, the filled fade-up and scale-in entrance animations from cl5-sme-002, static identity values on all five properties, and an endless opacity-only animation on the tags. It does not fix the width or padding cases. As an untested trade-off, an element with an endless decorative animation plus a static identity value such as translate 0 would fall back to the strict check and fail. Then add an undelayed endless scale that starts at identity, an endless spin and an endless width animation to the solved-run matrix. Correct the lab.json endless-animation sentence and the record's variant summary to match what the test does.

findings.claim: The new identity check still rejects some true identity values that Chromium reports. That runs against the loop-6 intent of accepting geometric identity end values. Line 149 accepts a rotate only when the parsed angle is exactly 0. In the pinned Chromium the rotate property keeps the authored angle in its computed value: rotate 360deg, 1turn, -360deg and 720deg compute to '360deg', '360deg', '-360deg' and '720deg', 'y 360deg' stays as written, and a zero axis ('0 0 0 45deg') is kept verbatim. Each draws the box exactly where and as large as without it (getBoundingClientRect unchanged), and identity() returns false. The equivalent transform: rotate(360deg), rotateY(360deg) and rotate3d(1, 2, 3, 1turn) compute to matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0) and are accepted. Full suite on 89161df6 with the private completed work: a static rotate of 360deg or 1turn on the tags fails task 11 only, with '... not by scaling, rotating, moving or zooming it'. A filled spin-in entrance ending at rotate 1turn fails the same way, while the same spin-in written with transform passes all 12. Also, DOMMatrixReadOnly.isIdentity (line 147) is an exact comparison, so floating-point residue such as rotate(120deg) applied three times (a matrix with entries of about 2.8e-16) is rejected; that case is contrived. Everything else checked behaves as intended. The probes covered transform none, the identity functions, matrix3d identity and perspective(none); scale 1, 1 1, 1 1 1 and 100%; rotate 0 with any unit or axis; translate 0, 0% and calc(10% - 10%); and zoom 1, 100%, normal, 0 and reset. All were accepted. Tiny values that Chromium serializes as non-zero were all rejected: translate 1e-7px, rotate 1e-7deg, scale 1.0001 and 0.99999, zoom 1.0001 and 0.99999, and a matrix offset of 1e-7. Only values below Chromium's six significant digits (for example scale or zoom 1.000001) serialize as 1 and pass, with a drawn change far under the 0.5px tolerance. No input made DOMMatrixReadOnly throw, including inline, display: none and display: contents tags with percentage translations. Low: fail-safe, unlikely, and the message names rotating.

evidence.section: Terminology: identity transform function (examples include rotate3d(1, 1, 1, 0), rotateX(0), rotateY(0), rotateZ(0)); 5 Individual Transform Properties, the rotate property (computed value: the keyword none, or an angle with an axis consisting of a list of three numbers; the axis keywords are equivalent to rotateX(), rotateY() and rotateZ())
Terminology: identity transform function (a transform function equivalent to an identity 4x4 matrix, e.g. rotate(0), matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0))
6 The DOMMatrix interfaces, DOMMatrixReadOnly attributes: isIdentity returns true only if m12, m13, m14, m21, m23, m24, m31, m32, m34, m41, m42 and m43 are 0 or -0 and m11, m22, m33 and m44 are 1

findings.recommendation: Build the rotate check from the rotation it describes, not from the angle text. Treat the rotate property as identity when its axis is the zero vector or its angle is a whole multiple of 360deg; or build new DOMMatrixReadOnly().rotateAxisAngleSelf(x, y, z, angle) and test it the same way as transform. Optionally compare matrices with a tolerance far below serialization precision (for example 1e-9) instead of exact isIdentity, so floating-point residue is accepted while every serialized tiny value is still rejected.

findings.claim: Since loop 6, the lab.json notes sentence 'It rejects the transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom properties.' is false as written: the test now accepts those properties at identity values. The completed work plus transform translate(0), scale 1, rotate 0deg, translate 0 0 and zoom 1 on both tags passed all 12 in 3 of 3 runs at 89161df6. The earlier clause in the same notes, 'it rejects scaling or zooming the checklist itself', also leaves out rotating and translating the checklist. README line 17 and the test's checklist message both name all four. This is maintainer-facing text, so the impact is small.
findings.recommendation: Reword the notes to match the test, for example: 'It rejects non-identity values of transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom on the tags and on the checklist itself; identity values such as a held animation end value are accepted.' Fix the cl6-sme-001 endless-animation sentence in the same edit.

items.note: Judged on wording, as the owner accepted this residual. README line 17 now ends 'It does not catch every animation, so task 11 also asks you to keep the checklist layout static.' Line 141 forbids any animation or transition that changes the size, position or scale of the checklist, the tags or any element around them that affects their layout, and allows decorative effects elsewhere. lab.json notes (line 87) say the test 'does not detect every animation that changes the drawn size later (for example a paused, delayed or very long one)'. The solved-run record lists paused, long-delayed, very long or slow animations and animated custom properties as not detected. That covers this finding's F, F2, G, G2 and S1-S4 classes. On 89161df6 with the completed work, a paused no-fill scale on the tags and a 5s-delayed endless scale both still pass all 12, as stated. Resolved for the finding as reported. The short, undelayed endless animations that loop 6 newly lets through are outside these lists and are raised separately as cl6-sme-001. The finding's classification by speed is not the real discriminator: an undelayed 0.5s endless width or padding animation also passes in most runs, at ea630d09 as well, because endless animations are read before their first frame. README line 17's general statement covers that too, so the learner-facing wording stays honest. The lab.json and record lists need the correction recommended in cl6-sme-001.

Lines 145-152 and 198 accept identity values. On 89161df6 with the completed work, full suite, these now pass all 12: a filled 0.4s fade-up with translate ending at 0 on the tags, a filled fade-up ending at transform none on the tags and the checklist, and a filled scale-in from .96 to 1 on .site-aside. Each passed in 3 of 3 runs at 89161df6 (and 3 of 3 on the work-dir copy patched as cl6-sme-001 recommends). Static identity values on all five properties also pass. Remaining identity rejections for the rotate property's full turns are raised as cl6-sme-002. The related, pre-existing case still fails mid-flight with 'something around it is scaling it', and that is fail-safe: a 1s no-fill entrance scale on the .page wrapper. README line 141 now forbids such motion on elements around the tags.

Variants (a) and (c) stay fixed on 89161df6 with the completed work. A forwards-filled animation holding .pack-tag-day at another width fails task 11 on the layout width, and one holding .pack-tag-overnight's padding fails on the padding check. Variant (b), an infinite keyframes animation that scales both tags, passes again. An endless alternating scale from 1 upward passed all 12 in 9 of 10 runs, and an endless pulse with only a to keyframe in 9 of 10, while both failed every run at ea630d09. The cause is the loop-6 identity acceptance combined with reading endless animations before their first frame (cl6-sme-001). Undelayed endless width or padding animations also pass in most runs, and did so already at ea630d09.

Line 152 reads .site-aside's transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom before pinning, and line 226 fails with the checklist message. On 89161df6 with the completed work, each of these fails task 11 only, with that message: a static zoom on .site-aside, a forwards-filled zoom animation on it, a zoom of 0.99, a translateX of 0.01px and a rotate of 0.001deg. zoom normal, 100%, 0 and reset compute to 1 and are accepted. The reported static case is closed. An endless pulse animation on .site-aside starting at scale 1 passes all 12 in 10 of 10 runs; that belongs to the animation class and is part of cl6-sme-001.

Lines 180-191 build the cause from what was detected, now including display none. On 89161df6 with the completed work, each fails task 11 only on the fill control, with a message naming the detected cause. Floated tags give '(it is floated)'. Absolutely positioned tags in a positioned checklist give '(it is positioned absolute)'. display: contents gives '(its display is contents, so it has no box of its own)'. display: none on .pack-tag-day gives '(its display is none, so it is hidden)'. README Troubleshooting line 208 lists contents and none. The self-contradictory 'its display is block' wording does not occur.
